original.description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept evolving HydRON services to maritime communications and identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap.Targeted Improvements:To enable maritime communications with satellite HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) systemDescription:Maritime routes are strategic in a connected world, where economies are interdependent. 80% of the global trade depends on shipping. Current strategical routes include South China, South India, Suez Canal, Mediterranean see, trans-Atlantic and Panama Canal. Together with the current routes, the transit along the arctic seais currently becoming more attention for cargo ships but also for defence purposes. Climate change may enable the use of this route,which could mean a drastic reduction in transport costs and service time (reduction of 25-40% in distance). From a logistics perspective, cargo companies aim to monitor their goods and containers, while ports seek to receive advance information about incoming cargo to optimize and plan the unloading process.Additional to the commercial and logistic interests, the defence aspects connected to maritime communications are of special interest, especially in an arctic route, where any developed infrastructure, could enhanceresilience.Currently, maritime communications relay on low-data rate satellite communications, or the use of low-band frequencies, when the ships are located close to shore. HydRON provides space-space and space-ground connectivity, extending terrestrial networksin space and providing global coverage.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements and system concepts for maritimecommunications (space-sea, sea-sea, sea-shore/ports), to extend the use of HydRON in maritime scenarios. Technology gaps and related technology roadmaps shall be developed, considering optical terminals and any critical technologies. The system shall consider themanagement of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a maritime ship-to-ship free-space network or hybrid communications with RF. The space segment shall consider the coverage along the most used routes. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be demonstrated. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

original.description: The increasing dependence on GNSS for positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services has highlighted vulnerabilities to jamming,spoofing, interference and space-weather effects. eLORAN is emerging as a resilient terrestrial complement to GNSS, but its adoptionrequires advanced tools capable of realistically testing and validating hybrid GNSS/eLORAN solutions. This activity will develop and validate a flexible, modular and future-proof eLORAN/GNSS signal simulator, synchronised with commercial GNSS simulators and supported by dedicated Receiver Analysis and Validation Tools. The simulator will provide high-fidelity signal generation, propagation modelling, multi-chain and multi-time-reference capabilities, and record-and-replay functions, enabling realistic end-to-end validation of resilient PNT solutions across timing, maritime and other application domains.

original.description: Objective:To characterise spacecraft materials that minimise atmospheric impacts during re-entry.Description:ESA's Green Agendaand Ecodesign Policy require that the environmental impacts of all space missions andprogrammes are assessed and reduced across their full life cycle. Launch and spacecraft re-entry effects onthe atmosphere are known gaps to fulfil these requirements. This results in significant uncertainty andsystematic exclusion of such effects when developing materials on the basis of sustainable performance.Previous and ongoing Discovery activities, Insights into the Chemistry of Atmospheric Re-entry of JunkedSpacecraft (ICARUS) and Impacts of space Debris ablation on Earth's Atmospheric System (IDEAS), havehighlighted the potential importance of ablation products in the atmosphere while established initial modellingapproaches and experimental validation capabilities.The proposed activity addresses this critical knowledge gap by developing a consolidated experimental andmodelling framework to characterise emissionsfrom spacecraft re-entry and integrate these into atmosphericand design assessment tools. This will enable the incorporation of atmospheric impacts into Life CycleAssessment (LCA) and support both Ecodesign and Design-for-Demise (D4D) decision making. Such aframework would be the first worldwide.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify representative launcher and spacecraftdemise-critical materials as well as Space Debris Particles(SPSs)- Propose material characterization factors (e.g. Ozon Depletionmetrics, radiative forcing proxies) andassociated quantification methodology- Refine methods to allow observation and characterization of particles generated during the vaporizationphase of selected materials- Demonstrate validation tests under realistic atmospheric re-entry conditions (e.g. Thermal, pressure andflow conditions) measuring and linking ablation fluxes to downstream chemical compositions- Parametrization and modelling of datasets for integration into re-entry and atmospheric chemistryclimatemodels-Define uncertainty and applicability ranges for model use- Formulate recommendations for standardised testing procedures to support the continuous developmentand population of material datasets.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME  RD organisations, preferably in cooperation. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

original.description: Strategic assessment activity to evaluate the readiness of artificial intelligence to support Earth system science and future ESA Earth Observation missions. The activity will assess AI approaches across the EO Science Strategy and its Overarching Science Themes,with a focus on identifying where AI is already delivering credible scientific value, where important scientific and technical gapsremain, and where maturity is sufficient to support mission-facing tasks such as geophysical observables retrieval development, observation requirement definition, observing-system analysis, and science-gap identification. It will build a structured evidence base, assess scientific rigour and mission relevance, and develop an AI readiness framework aligned with ESA readiness principles, leadingto a roadmap for FutureEO investments and follow-on actions. A core outcome of the study is a decision-ready assessment of where AIcan credibly strengthen future EO mission science and planning, and where further evidence or development is still required.
